chapters.title: Teaching capability and field instruction
chapters.summary: Provost support established drone and visualization capacity for teaching. Callicoon fieldwork, Lamont course sessions, research training and educator workshops connect field observation with spatial analysis.

chapters.title: Community-engaged mapping
chapters.summary: SDEV4650 connects students, the Staten Island Urban Center and community partners around waterfront questions. The work extends from the 60 Hannah Street field session to later North Shore mapping and partner access to spatial information.

chapters.title: NYC Parks UAS research
chapters.summary: EFPL’s developing NYC Parks portfolio includes repeated Four Sparrow Marsh surveys, North Shore Esplanade and Morningside Park mapping, and forthcoming work at Highbridge Park. North Shore also continues the Staten Island community partnership.

chapters.title: HOT, UNZA and mapping in Zambia
chapters.summary: Work with the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team and University of Zambia colleagues connects international exchange, field methods and selected-site mapping around Mtukuzi. Fieldwork also contributed to a learning module developed for TOPSTSCHOOL.

chapters.title: Current research and forthcoming work
chapters.summary: At Lamont, terrain and surface information support investigation of wind dynamics alongside field measurements. Ongoing Morningside research, methods development and forthcoming Highbridge work extend the program with partners.

case_studies.title: Callicoon student fieldwork
case_studies.summary: SDEV3450 students collected drone observations and developed spatial analyses during a two-day field exercise led by Kytt MacManus and teaching assistant Juan Nathaniel.
case_studies.question: How can students connect field observations with spatial analysis?
case_studies.contribution: Field exercises in nighttime lights, terrain, vegetation and 3D modeling, followed by a jointly produced student StoryMap.
case_studies.credit: CIESIN · Columbia University · Kytt MacManus · Juan Nathaniel · SDEV3450 students
case_studies.details: The 2021 Provost Emerging Technology Grant supported equipment for Drones and AR/VR for 3D Modeling in GIS. Earth Institute Course Support funded travel and accommodation. These were distinct forms of support.

case_studies.title: Repeated mapping at Four Sparrow Marsh
case_studies.summary: EFPL and Natan Charytan use repeated drone surveys to document marsh conditions in an ecological and restoration research setting.
case_studies.question: How can repeated spatial observations support study of a restored marsh?
case_studies.contribution: Permitted UAS observations, orthomosaics, elevation products and reconstructed surface views for continued research.
case_studies.credit: EFPL · Columbia University · Natan Charytan · NYC Parks
case_studies.details: The April 18, 2025 operation was the first UAS flight approved by NYC Parks, according to Kytt MacManus’s first-hand project account. Wind curtailed that operation; the team returned on May 2. Repeated surveys provide observations for research, while registered comparisons and independent accuracy evaluation are separate tasks.

case_studies.title: Lamont terrain and wind research
case_studies.summary: EFPL investigates how terrain and surface geometry can inform interpretation of wind observations and airflow modeling at Lamont.
case_studies.question: How do terrain and surface features help us interpret local wind dynamics?
case_studies.contribution: Spatial surface information and field instrumentation for research alongside meteorological and Doppler LiDAR observations.
case_studies.credit: EFPL · Columbia Engineering · DURIP-supported instrumentation · ARO research
case_studies.details: DURIP supported the IF1200A purchase for an ARO project. The interactive Lamont point sample is photogrammetric surface reconstruction. A separate March 24, 2026 LiDAR plate uses relative coordinates because its LAS CRS label conflicts with coordinate magnitudes. Neither display establishes independent accuracy or validates a wind model.

cover.title: Lamont point cloud: oblique view
cover.caption: A decimated visualization of the archived photogrammetric point cloud from 603 LAS tiles totaling 16,541,307 source points. Oblique projection with exaggerated vertical scale, colored by source elevation.
cover.uncertainty: Photogrammetric surface points, not bare-earth terrain or a wind field. Processing report identifies UTM18N and EGM96; independent accuracy not established.

visuals.title: Lamont LiDAR point-cloud display
visuals.caption: Plan and oblique views of a subsampled existing IF1200A LiDAR point cloud at Lamont. Colors represent relative height in source coordinate units.
visuals.uncertainty: Relative-coordinate display only: LAS header CRS EPSG:4326 conflicts with the UTM18n filename and projected-coordinate magnitudes. 140,012 display points are sampled from 71,265,603 stored points. No absolute accuracy, bare-earth classification, or validated wind model is claimed.
